narrative.overview:
Every Altvane plug-in is announced the way a concert in a Swiss poster series is: one cool white sheet, lowercase grotesk set flush left on a strict twelve-column grid, and one large geometric figure. The figure is not illustration. It is computed from the product's real mechanism (EQ's filter response as concentric arcs, Dialogue's stems summing to the input, the Compressor's gain computer as columns under a knee, the Limiter's lookahead holding a waveform under its ceiling), it draws in once from the product's neutral state, and it answers the pointer and the keyboard. The sheet carries the precision claim; the figure proves it.

The page is quiet and dense in the way a printed programme is dense: near-black ink, hairline rules, registration ticks on every column line, small tabular readings with the condition they were measured under. Hierarchy comes from Archivo's width axis and from scale, not from colour, boxes or weight. Each product owns exactly one printed spot ink, and that ink appears only in its figure, its own rules and the links that name it. Actions are set type standing on a rule with a drawn arrow; nothing on the sheet is a filled button.

The world rejects the plug-in category's defaults: a dark hero, a GUI screenshot used as the hook, feature cards and format badges. Screenshots do appear, but only further down a product page, framed as a plate.
keyCharacteristics: Cool white stock, near-black ink, one spot ink per product.
Archivo Variable across its width axis: expanded and light for names, normal for text, tabular figures for readings.
Twelve-column sheet with registration ticks; figures crop off the right edge of the sheet.
Hairline rules everywhere; a 1.5px rule heads every list, table and product section.
No boxes: actions are type on a rule; lists and tables are ruled, never carded.
One authored motion: the figure's draw-in, plus underline wipes in the spot ink.

rules.name: The One Spot Ink Rule
rules.body: Each product owns one spot ink, used for that product's figure, its 1.5px section rule and its hover wipes, and nothing else. A spot ink only ever marks its own product: where another product is named (a header nav link, a programme row, a "Next" action), that element wipes in the named product's ink, never the page's.

rules.name: The Spot Never Sets Text Rule
rules.body: Spot inks are for marks, rules and fills, never for type. Dialogue Vermilion is 3.59:1 on the stock: enough for a graphic, not for words.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Text is set in Programme Ink, Second Ink or Third Ink, and nothing lighter. Hairlines are for rules only.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by width before weight: 125% for display, 112% to 118% for names, titles, actions and the wordmark, 100% for reading text. Never use bold weights to make something louder; make it wider and larger.

rules.name: The Lowercase Poster Rule
rules.body: Display and headline sizes are set lowercase via text-transform; title size and below keep sentence case so product names stay readable.

rules.name: The Reading Rule
rules.body: Every number on the sheet is set in tabular lining figures and carries the condition it was measured under. A value with an adjective instead of a condition does not belong in a reading.

rules.name: The Twelve Columns Rule
rules.body: Every element starts and ends on a column line. If a placement cannot be written as `grid-column: a / span b` on the sheet, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Crop Rule
rules.body: Figures are large enough to be cut by the sheet's edge. They do not sit centred in a box with margin around them.

rules.name: The Printed Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the sheet casts a shadow except a screenshot of a real window. No cards, panels or sticky bars float.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Corners are square unless the object is a circle by geometry or a picture of something outside the sheet.

dos: **Do** give every product surface its spot ink through `data-product`, and use it only for the figure, the 1.5px section rule and hover wipes.
**Do** set actions as type on a rule with a drawn arrow: 1.5px Programme Ink for primary, 1px Strong Hairline for quiet.
**Do** carry hierarchy on Archivo's width axis (125% display, 112% names and titles, 100% text), going lighter as type gets larger.
**Do** place every element on the twelve-column sheet and let figures crop at the sheet's edge.
**Do** head every list, table and section with a 1.5px rule and separate rows with 1px hairlines.
**Do** compute every figure from the product's real mechanism, and keep it complete and static without JavaScript or under reduced motion.
**Do** set every number in tabular lining figures with the condition it was measured under.
donts: **Don't** fill a button or draw a box around an action.
**Don't** set text in a spot ink, or in any colour lighter than Third Ink (#6b6d70).
**Don't** use a product's spot ink for anything that is not that product's figure, rule or link.
**Don't** use cards, panels, format badges or a dark section; group content with rules instead.
**Don't** add shadows or rounded corners to anything except a screenshot plate (6px) or a key cap (3px).
**Don't** lead a page with a GUI screenshot; the figure is the hook, and screenshots sit lower on product pages as plates.
**Don't** add motion beyond the figure's single draw-in and the underline and arrow responses to hover.
**Don't** add a symbol or logo mark beside the wordmark, and don't use the `libs/ui` weather-vane mark or the plug-ins' Inter typeface on the website.
